note:
PARAMETER MAP, read off braids/digital_oscillator.cc. Line 1209, `parameter_0 = 172 - (parameter_[0] >> 8)`: parameter_[0] is Braids' TIMBRE, and it is BOW FORCE -- the scaler on the friction argument at line 1259 -- read INVERTED, so TIMBRE 0 gives 172 (the steepest bow table, least grip, the bow slips) and TIMBRE 1 gives 45 (most grip, hardest scrape). Line 1210, `parameter_1 = 6 + (parameter_[1] >> 9)`: parameter_[1] is COLOR, and it is BOW POSITION -- the bridge-tap fraction of the loop at line 1220 -- read rising, COLOR 0 giving 6/256 and COLOR 1 giving 69/256. RenderBowed uses no INTERPOLATE_PARAMETER macro at all, so both are read raw and neither is smoothed. So p1 maps to the engine's TIMBRE and p2 to its HARMONICS, and every case below pins one of the two at an end while the other moves: swapping them renders plausibly either way, which is exactly how the same misreading shipped in fold.

CASE-ID WARNING. `pressure-hard` is TIMBRE 0.0, which is the LIGHTEST bow force (parameter_0 = 172), and `pressure-light` is TIMBRE 1.0, the HEAVIEST. The ids read off parameter_0's magnitude, not off the physical quantity, and are therefore backwards against the engine's own control copy ('Increases bow pressure from a thin whistle to a hard scrape'). They are kept for continuity with the port notes; read the case names, not the ids.

MORPH SITS AT 1.0 IN EVERY CASE, NOT AT 0.5. bowed_engine.cc's `nut_gain = 0.55f + 0.45f * morph` sums to exactly 1.0f, so Braids' welded `nut_reflection = -nut_value` (line 1252, gain exactly 1.0) is at MORPH 1.0. The port's added nut axis is one-sided -- it can only choke the nut below the module, never open it further -- so its stock position is the top of the range and not the detent. That is legal because MORPH has no detent (SPEC section 2); MACRO does, and MACRO is stock at 0.5, where ApplyMacro(0, -12, 12, 0.5) returns 0 semitones and the body biquad reduces to Braids' kBiquadPole1/kBiquadPole2 up to the 0.94% error in kBowedStockTheta.

NO CENTS TOLERANCE ANYWHERE. BOWD is a stick-slip self-oscillator, not an oscillator: its pitch is the limit cycle of a nonlinear feedback loop, and the 4.61-cent kCorrectedSampleRate offset every port here carries is enough to settle it into a neighbouring cycle. The corrected figure is still printed and still worth reading -- a whole-semitone reading would mean an R5 rate bug -- but it is not a pass/fail metric for this engine. Measured across the grid below it stays inside +-3 cents.

TOLERANCES. acRmsDb 5.0 and spectrumDb 4.0, uniform, UNCHANGED from the run that failed. They are looser than the ~1 dB / ~1.5 dB house target for two written reasons. (1) LEVEL: the port declares a 1.6x make-up Braids does not have, which is +4.08 dB before SoftClip compresses it unevenly. (2) SPECTRUM: a chaotic self-oscillator settles into a different cycle for a sub-cent pitch difference. Nothing here was widened to make a case pass; the six cases that used to fail were fixed in the DSP.

THE DEFECT THESE CASES CAUGHT, AND ITS FIX (2026-07). Six cases -- pressure-hard, pressure-thin, corner-hard-bridge, low-at-bridge, firm-pressure and mid-neck -- used to fail from +7.9 to +37.2 dB AC RMS. CAUSE: Braids' fractional-delay read is `Mix(a, b, frac) << 8` (line 1247) against int8 line storage, and stmlib::Mix (stmlib/utils/dsp.h:86) is `(a * (65535 - balance) + b * balance) >> 16` returning an int16 -- the interpolation between the two taps is FLOORED to whole int8 counts, 1/128 of full scale, before the shift -- while the shipped port interpolated in float. That truncation is a loss term inside the feedback loop and it is what lets the module's bow SLIP. The port now reproduces the integer expression (MixInt8 in bowed_engine.cc, verified bit-exact against stmlib::Mix over the whole int8 x int8 x balance domain), and ALL FIFTEEN CASES THAT DECLARE A TOLERANCE AGREE: level -2.88 to +4.89 dB, spectra 0.05 to 2.01 dB. high-bridge-clamp declares none and still counts as neither.

SCOPE OF THE DEFECT, measured rather than assumed, and worth keeping on record because it is what a user will hear change. Braids is BISTABLE along TIMBRE, not uniformly quiet at the light end: at note 45, COLOR 0.5 it renders -44.1 / -18.4 / -41.3 / -19.1 / -18.0 / -15.1 / -13.2 / -10.3 dBFS at TIMBRE 0 / .1 / .2 / .3 / .4 / .5 / .7 / 1, collapsing in bands (TIMBRE 0 to .075 and .175 to .225) and bowing normally between them. The shipped port was flat across that axis (-14.2 to -7.5 dBFS) and missed every collapse; AND the defect was not confined to low TIMBRE -- over a 36-point note x COLOR x TIMBRE grid it broke this file's 5 dB tolerance at 13 points, worst note 24 / TIMBRE 0.5 / COLOR 0.0 at +37.2 dB, MID bow force. The fixed port collapses where the module collapses: -41.4 dBFS at note 45 / TIMBRE 0 (was -14.2, Braids -44.1) and -46.4 at note 24 / TIMBRE 0.5 / COLOR 0 (was -11.9, Braids -49.1).

ISOLATION, kept for the record. Restoring the Mix truncation ALONE greens all sixteen cases. Rebuilding with Braids' int8 WRAP instead of the port's saturation moves every point of the 36-point grid by less than 0.06 dB, and so does flooring the friction curve to Braids' integer table -- the truncation was the whole of it. Two smaller quantisation corrections shipped alongside it anyway, each under 0.4 dB on every case here EXCEPT high-bridge-clamp, which the clamp change carries from +7.96 dB / 12.69 dB to +3.45 dB / 0.62 dB: the friction closed form is now FLOORED to the 1/32768 grid the table holds (floor matches all 257 entries, round matches 137; the float32 closed form then reproduces 255 of the 256 reachable indices exactly, index 27 alone one LSB high), and the bridge-tap clamp dropped from 2.0 to 1.0 samples and moved ahead of the neck split.

WHAT MOVED FOR A USER, which is not the same question as which cases pass. Braids is fixed, so each case's change in AC RMS delta IS the port's own level change. Seven cases move under 0.7 dB (stock, pressure-light, bow-at-bridge, bow-up-neck, corner-light-neck, low, high-clean), retrigger 1.0, octave-fold 1.6, mid-neck 4.8, firm-pressure 5.5, and the five collapse or dead corners 19 to 33 dB. firm-pressure and mid-neck are ORDINARY bowing settings -- Braids renders -16.4 and -17.5 dBFS there, nothing collapses -- so the change is not confined to the collapse bands, and copy that says otherwise is wrong.

RESIDUAL, outside these cases: at note 60 / TIMBRE 0.4 / COLOR 0.5 the fixed port settles an OCTAVE above Braids and reads 4.5-6.0 dB of octave-band spectrum, past this file's own 4.0 dB figure, where the pre-fix port read 1.6-1.7. No case samples that point. It is limit-cycle relocation rather than a regression in kind (the same knife edge sits at COLOR 0.45 pre-fix, an octave the other way), and over the 36-point grid the fix takes points past 4 dB from four to one and the worst from 10.7 to 4.5.

cases.name: TIMBRE at 0.0 -- least grip, parameter_0 = 172, where Braids' bow slips
TIMBRE at 0.2 -- inside the slipping regime, not at its end
COLOR at 0.0 -- bow hard against the bridge, parameter_1 = 6
COLOR at 1.0 -- bow well up the neck, parameter_1 = 69
Both axes at one corner: least grip, at the bridge
The opposite corner: most grip, up the neck
Bottom of the keyboard, long delay lines
Below the fold floor, where both sides halve the delay -- MIDI 4, not 21
High note with the bow off the bridge, where no tap is clamped
The same high note at the bridge -- the clamped-tap corner, dead on both sides
Low note with the bow at the bridge -- MID bow force, and the worst point found
TIMBRE at 0.75 -- the UPPER half of the bow-force axis
A third note with the bow up the neck
Struck twice a second -- Braids memsets both delay lines on strike, the port Resets

caseNotes.octave-fold: The fold floor is 9.4 to 12.6 Hz depending on COLOR -- 11.44 Hz at COLOR 0 where the NECK tap overflows first, 12.64 Hz at COLOR 1 where the BRIDGE tap does, and a minimum of 9.38 Hz at parameter_1 = 51 where the two thresholds cross -- so it is NOT reachable at MIDI 21: at MIDI 21 and COLOR 1 the bridge tap is 470 of 1023 and the neck tap 1273 of 4095, and nothing halves. tests/scenarios.json's scenario of that name renders at MIDI 21 and is misnamed. This case uses MIDI 4 with COLOR 1, where Braids' loop at digital_oscillator.cc:1222 and the port's at bowed_engine.cc:135 each halve exactly once.
caseNotes.high-bridge-clamp: NO TOLERANCE DECLARED, on purpose, and kept that way: both sides are dead here -- Braids falls to -61.0 dBFS and stops entirely after the attack -- so any ratio measured here is the ratio of two residuals rather than a fidelity measurement, whichever way it comes out. This case does NOT count among the agreeing cases. It is kept because it is the only coverage of the port's clamped bridge tap. It used to read +22.8 dB level / 10.7 dB spectrum, because the port sustained a -40 dBFS whistle where Braids died, and because the clamp floor was 2.0 samples applied AFTER neck_delay had been taken from delay -- so it lengthened the whole loop and rendered flat from MIDI 72.9 upward, a full octave below the MIDI 84.5 at which Braids' own tap drops under one sample. The floor is now 1.0 samples, exactly where Braids goes degenerate, and it is applied BEFORE the neck split so it moves the tap within the loop instead of lengthening it. The port now reads -59.0 dBFS here, 0.62 dB of spectrum from Braids.
caseNotes.low-at-bridge: Added by the audit pass, and the largest divergence found anywhere on the grid: Braids slips here at MID bow force (-49.1 dBFS at note 24 / TIMBRE 0.5 / COLOR 0.0) and the shipped port sustained -11.9, +37.2 dB. It is the case that falsified 'the defect is the low-TIMBRE half of the axis'. The original twelve cases swept each axis end only at note 45, and swept notes only at COLOR 0.5, so this corner was unsampled. With the Mix truncation restored the port renders -46.4 dBFS here and the case passes at +4.16 dB.
caseNotes.firm-pressure: Added by the audit pass, to sample the UPPER half of the bow-force axis, which the original grid skipped between TIMBRE 0.5 and 1.0. It failed at +7.9 dB before the Mix truncation was restored -- so the divergence was never a light-bow phenomenon -- and passes at +2.39 dB now.
caseNotes.mid-neck: Added by the audit pass. A third note at COLOR 1.0; the original grid only visited COLOR 1.0 at notes 45, 84 and 4. It failed at +8.4 dB before the fix and passes at +3.62 dB now.
caseNotes.retrigger: Added by the audit pass, and it passed both before and after the fix (+4.91 dB then, +3.90 dB now). It is the only case that exercises the reset path, which is worth pinning for this engine specifically: DigitalOscillator::Init() memsets state_ but NOT delay_lines_, and RenderBowed reads delay_lines_, so the delay lines are only cleared by its own `if (strike_)` branch (digital_oscillator.cc:1203). The port's Reset() clears both lines and every filter state on TRIGGER_RISING_EDGE, and the agreement here says the two strike behaviours match.
